objections.claim_attacked: chosen_intervention: PR #7650 fixes the congestion issue and the report-update follow-up is part of the same resolution
objections.objection: The thread separates two related defects: PR #7650 is claimed to fix the congestion issue, while the follow-up only says the reporter will work on updating the congestion report when a net is deleted; the record therefore cannot treat the nonexistent-net marker/report staleness as already fixed by PR #7650.

mechanism_check: HOLDS — a merged-net incremental-groute fix plausibly explains why a net erased by repair_timing would leave bogus congestion and why refreshing merged-net handling would let GRT pass, though the exact PR #7650 mechanism is not described in this thread.
evidence_check: ASSERT — post_state is only the reporter closing with 'sounds like it was resolved', with no rerun metric proving zero overflow, clean DRCs, runtime, or disappearance of the stale marker.
attribution_check: SUPPORTS — the direct quote carries eder-matheus, a 2025-06-25 date, and the issue locator, and it directly supports the narrow claim that PR #7650 was intended to fix the observed congestion issue.
missing_from_story: The actual PR #7650 summary/diff and whether it changed incremental groute merged-net handling, congestion-report refresh, or both
Whether the separate 'update congestion report when a net is deleted' work landed and in which commit/PR
A post-fix rerun on the same asap7 cva6 hierarchical-synth setup showing GRT passes, with overflow/DRC/runtime numbers
Confirmation that the DRC-viewer/congestion-report marker no longer references the deleted/merged net
Whether RUDY and GRT agree after the fix or whether the RUDY disagreement was a separate model mismatch
Repair_timing before/after buffer insert/remove counts and the identity of the merged net pair, if recoverable
most_defensible_part: The eder-matheus direct quote naming PR #7650 plus the merged-net explanation is the strongest element: it gives a concrete fix reference and a coherent reason a post-repair_timing net could be absent from ODB while still appearing in congestion output.
